name: Meeting someone
blurb: Where you are from, who you came with, and what you do not follow yet.

items.note: から marks where you started — the same particle as a train from Kyoto, used of a person. どこ stays where the answer would go rather than moving to the front.
来 is the stem of 来ます, so 来 + ました is 'came'. The place still takes から, exactly as in the question it answers.
お名前 is the polite form of 名前 — you use it of someone else's name, never your own. 何 sits where the answer will go rather than moving to the front.
This と is 'with', not the 'and' that joins a coffee and a cake. Same tile, and which one it is depends on whether a verb follows.
も replaces は here rather than sitting beside it: 私も, never 私はも. Two tiles and です is a whole turn in a conversation.

items.ans: 日本語|が|分かり|ません
items.note: 分かる takes が for a state of being that is understood, not を which requires an active physical action
